phases.title: Bend a sine — Start opposite source slopes at a zero opening
notes: Source phase zero and a steady index of three open the bent wave at zero. The source initially rises; the derivative with respect to carrier phase is four at the opening.
Half a source cycle still opens the bent wave at zero, within floating-point error. The source initially falls; with index three the opening derivative is minus two.
The source completes two cycles per carrier cycle. Phase zero still opens at zero, but the opening derivative is seven. A shared opening is not a shared slope.
phases.facts: Toy y(theta)=sin(theta+I*sin(q*theta+2*pi*p)). Here I=3, theta0=0, p=0/.5/0 and q=1/1/2. y0=0/sin(3*sin(pi))/0; numerical middle is3.6739403974420594e-16. dy/dtheta at0=cos(I*sin(2*pi*p))*(1+I*q*cos(2*pi*p))=4,-2,7. Derivatives are per radian of carrier phase, not voltage/time measurements. Existing native ratios1/2, phase0/.5, index3 exist; apply steady,moment0. Preserve finite envelope.
